l: Wrath-demon of rapine, Yasna, Yasna XLVIII.
s: The Wrath-demon of rapine is among the forces to be cast down in the coming struggle.

The refuge is to be held fast by those abiding by the Good Mind and the Righteous Order. The bounteous man belongs to its sacred bond, and Ahura Mazda's struggling saint is to be placed there in His world.

The holy Reign is sought through potent prayer, along with its sacred reward and blessing. The speaker asks how to seek helpers for spreading and maintaining it while living through the Good Spirit's deeds.
The Saoshyant is expected to see the wonder-working grace of the Good Mind and to discern how gifts of recompense may be his own.

l: men of mind's perfection, Yasna, Yasna XLVIII.
s: The men of mind's perfection are awaited as those who will drive away the polluted drunken joy that empowers the Karpans and supports tyrannical rule.
The Karpans use angry zeal to crush the faithful, and their inspiration supports the evil rule of the tyrants of the provinces. Their polluted drunken joy is to be driven away.

l: tyrants of the provinces, Yasna, Yasna XLVIII.
s: The tyrants of the provinces maintain evil rule through the inspiration associated with the Karpans. The unit asks when this rule will be ended.
The provinces are subject to tyrants' evil rule and are to receive Saviours. The Saviours will act for the provinces through the Good Mind, the Righteous Order, and Ahura Mazda's commandments.
Perfected Piety is awaited together with the Righteousness. She is expected to come with the amenities of home and pastures for the Kine and to bring relief from cruel people of evil life and faith.

l: Saviours of the Provinces, Yasna, Yasna XLVIII.
s: The Saviours of the Provinces will advance through the Good Mind's grace and mental keenness. They will perform every deed of Ahura Mazda's commandment with the help of and in accordance with the Holy Order, serving as steadfast foes of hate.

The conflicts are future struggles in which the speaker seeks strength and courage as leader of the tribes. They are associated with the hoped-for defeat of evil heretics, the Demon-of-the-Lie, rapine, envy, and oppressive rulers.

Yasna XLIX concerns opposition from Bendva, appeals to Ahura Mazda for help through Good Mind and Righteousness, and the struggle between the faithful and the wicked. It rejects those who support Wrath of Rapine and the Daêvas, while praising those who guard Faith and live according to the Holy Order. Frashaostra is given headship of the Holy Order, and Gâmâspa and the “hero” are joined in the best recompense. The souls of evil men are destined for the Lie’s abode.
Yasna XLIX presents reverses and hopes, addressing Bendva’s opposition, appeals to Ahura Mazda, the roles of Frashaostra and other chiefs, and the fates of the faithful and wicked.

Bendva has continually fought against the speaker and is described as powerful enough to crush his strength. Bendva is estranged from the Righteous Order, has not maintained or strengthened Piety, and does not seek insight through Good Mind.

Ahura Mazda is asked to provide gifts of good, bring about Bendva’s death, shelter the people through Good Mind, and reveal the truths and Faith that should be proclaimed. Ahura Mazda is also asked to confirm Frashaostra’s headship and grant sheltering headship to the speaker.
Frashaostra has been given the guardian power and headship of the Holy Order by Ahura Mazda. The speaker asks that this gracious gift be confirmed to him.

l: Gâmâspa the Hvôgva, Yasna, Yasna XLIX.
s: Gâmâspa is joined with the “hero” in the best recompense and in the course of the Holy Order.

The wicked scheme with evil will, support Wrath of Rapine and the Daêvas, and are associated with evil words and consciences. The speaker abjures the allies of the wicked, and the wicked are destined for evil food and dwelling in the Lie’s abode.

Righteousness is invoked as the means by which the disaffected may be won back and as the Holy Order that protects and saves the religious choice. Righteousness speaks within the Mãthra about the intention of the divine will.
Good Mind is asked to bring about Bendva’s death, provide sheltering leadership, and help discern and proclaim the truths of the Faith. Its power enables the faithful to guard Faith.
Piety is described as bountiful and perfect, but Bendva has not maintained or strengthened it. Piety exists through Âramaiti and is associated with self-humbling praises and sacrificing zeal.
Faith is to be proclaimed together with the pure Daêna as the Faith of Ahura Mazda. The faithful guard it against Wrath of Rapine, and only believing natures are to join in the best recompense.

l: Wrath-demon of rapine, Yasna, Yasna XLIX.
s: Wrath of Rapine is supported by those who scheme and will evil, together with her Râma. The faithful are described as guarding Faith against her.
The Daêvas are settled and supported by those whose will and deeds are evil. Their support is identified as the wicked’s perverted Faith and Insight.
The Lie is associated with the Demon-of-the-Lie, who deals wounds to the evil judge. Its abode is the dwelling place destined for the souls of evil men.
Bendva’s death is requested from Ahura Mazda through the power of Good Mind as an answer to the speaker’s sorrow and opposition.

The speaker, the supplicant, asks Ahura Mazda what aids of grace are granted through the Righteous Order and Good Mind. The unit concerns the protection of flocks, herds, the Kine, and lands, and calls for righteous settlers and servants to bring prosperity and justice. Zarathustra and other Mãthra-speakers are urged to proclaim and teach the righteous way and the regulations of Ahura Mazda. The speaker offers sacrifice, worship, Yasnas, praises, and prayer, seeking the path to the Home-of-song and help for the cause.

Ahura Mazda is invoked as the Great Creator and Lord who grants aids of grace, blessings, lands, protection, and help through the Righteous Order and Good Mind. Ahura Mazda advances with friendliness, gives visible relief, and is praised through the speaker’s worship and Yasnas.
Zarathustra is identified as the faithful friend who lifts his voice in Mãthras. He is urged to proclaim and teach the righteous way and the regulations in accordance with the Good Mind.

l: the speaker (the supplicant), Yasna, Yasna XLIX, 12-L.
s: The speaker asks for grace, protection, righteous lands, and assistance for the cause. The speaker offers sacrifice, worship, Yasnas, praises, and prayer, and seeks to become a supplicant who gains his ends and reaches the Home-of-song.

The Righteous Order is presented as a source of grace, protection, justice, prosperity, and the right path. It enables the speaker and others to act righteously, obtain lands, and approach Ahura Mazda in worship.
The Good Mind is given within the speaker’s soul and provides grace, understanding, good virtue, and guidance. It supports the proclamation of regulations and makes holy works worthy and radiant.

l: Divine Sovereign Power, Yasna, Yasna XLIX, 12-L.
s: The Sovereign Authority is associated with Ahura Mazda and with the gift granted through the Righteous Order. Its help enables the wisher to stand upon the certain pathway.
The Kine is described as the joy-creating living symbol of peace. The text asks how she may be protected, provided with pastures, and secured for the welfare of the land.

The speaker asks Ahura Mazda to grant lands that live in justice and openly display the many splendours of the sun. These lands are to be sought and gained for the cause, and a righteous heroic settler may make an imperilled farm flourish near the foeman’s fields.
The Home-of-song is the place where the speaker expects to hear the praises of offering saints who see Ahura Mazda’s face. The speaker seeks to reach it through worship and the certain pathway.
The Mãthra-word is spoken by servants who are cheered by Ahura Mazda’s friendly and visible relief. Its speaker can bring the people onward and settle them in weal and bliss.

Mãthra-speakers are urged and yoked for their sacred course toward the Bridges where adoration is complete. They proclaim the righteous way and are joined with the Righteous Order and Good Mind for help.

Sacrifice and worship are offered to Ahura Mazda together with the Righteous Order, Good Mind, and Sovereign Authority. Through them, the speaker approaches Ahura Mazda with supplication, raised hands, sacred metric feet, and freely-giving service.

Yasnas are offered as sacrifices through which the speaker approaches and praises Ahura Mazda and the Righteous Order. They are also described as means by which the speaker may hear the praises of offering saints in the Home-of-song.

Praises are offered to Ahura Mazda, the Righteous Order, and the Good Mind in sacrifice and worship. Stars, suns, and the Aurora are described as shining works that speak the praise of the Great Giver through the Righteous Order.
Prayer consists of the speaker’s requests for grace, protection, righteous lands, guidance, and help for the cause. The speaker makes prayer with praises, supplication, and hands stretched out.

The unit is an appeal to Ahura Mazda and the Assembly of the Faithful for Good Government, Sovereign Power, wealth, salvation, and spiritual blessings through Asha, Good Mind, and Âramaiti. It presents Zarathustra as the speaker and asks who supports him, while praising Kavi Vîstâspa, Frashaostra, Gâmâspa, and others associated with the great cause and the good Religion. It contrasts the rewards of the righteous with the punishment of the wicked and the Lie, and describes the Kine, waters, and plants as creations requiring protection. It also speaks of judgment at the Kinvat Bridge, the consequences of sacrifice and worship, and the promised blessings of Ahura Mazda.

Ahura Mazda is invoked as the foremost guide and light, the source of Good Government, Sovereign Power, wealth, Immortality, Welfare, salvation, and blessings. He rewards those who give to the good citizen and punishes the withholder of sacrifice, and He is said to enter the Song Home first.

Zarathustra is the speaker who appeals to Ahura Mazda and speaks for the assembled faithful. He is described as upright from earliest days, untouched by impurity, and associated with the good Religion and the great cause.

Kavi Vîstâspa is said to have attained wisdom in the great cause through the chants of Good Mind and to have received the wisdom Ahura Mazda conceived in accordance with Asha. He is also said to have established Sovereign Power and granted it to Maidhyô-mâh the Spitâma.
Asha is the Righteous Order that opposes oppressive actions and guides the faithful. It is invoked for help, is associated with upright action and salvation, and is to be made firm through Good Mind.
Good Mind inspires and guides, speaks through the Mãthra, and reveals words and doctrine. It is associated with Sovereign Power, wisdom, salvation, and the government of the kingdom.
Âramaiti is identified with Piety and is asked to approach, grant blessings, and speak her truths. She is also associated with Kavi Vîstâspa, who is called a man of Âramaiti.
Sovereign Power is sought as the best rule and defense, established through Good Mind. It is requested for the preservation of desired wealth and is attributed to Kavi Vîstâspa's gift.

The Kine are created along with the waters and plants and are objects of prayer and protection. The tiller of the earth seeks them and the wealth in herds through Asha, while the Karpans are condemned for failing to provide complete pasture for them.

l: Good Government (of Ahura), Yasna, Yasna LI.
s: Good Government of Ahura is to be chosen above wished-for things because it brings happiness and opposes oppressive actions through Asha and pious zeal. The speaker asks Ahura Mazda to help bring it about at every hour.

l: the Assembly of the Faithful, Yasna, Yasna LI.
s: The Assembly of the Faithful is addressed as the gathered people who hear Ahura Mazda and seek guidance. The speaker appeals to them concerning loyalty to Zarathustra, the good Religion, Asha, and the great cause.
The wicked receive what is worse than evil when they withhold sacrifice and reject the holy rule. Their conscience and spirit face punishment, and they are wounded by the sword of justice.

The righteous are those who maintain Asha in the community and in the soul and act uprightly. They receive salvation, blessings, and a joyful destiny, while their conscience crushes the wicked at judgment.
The Lie is the opposing creation to the good rule and is associated with miscreants, false teachings, and the Home of the Lie. Those led by the Karpans are delivered there by their doctrines.
The good Religion is associated with wisdom, correct laws, the true life, Asha, and the great cause. The people are urged to receive it with desire for the gaining of Asha.
The Kinvat Bridge is the place of judgment where the righteous man's conscience crushes the wicked man's spirit. The wicked spirit struggles to reach and pollute Asha's paths there.

Sacrifice is offered to Ahura Mazda's cause with homage and praise. The one who withholds sacrifice receives worse than evil, while the Immortals are asked to accept sacrifice and seek Ahura Mazda's grace.

Worship is performed through wise, self-humbling devotion, praise, homage, and drawing near to the eternal ones. It is supported by Good Mind and directed toward Ahura Mazda and those who have ever lived and still live.

l: the cause of Righteousness, Yasna, Yasna LI.
s: The great cause is the religious cause associated with Asha, Good Mind, the good Religion, and Sovereign Power. Kavi Vîstâspa and other faithful figures are described as attaining wisdom or acting in support of it.

Wealth is requested as desired prosperity to be granted and preserved under Sovereign Power. It is linked with the Kine, herds, the tiller of the earth, and the blessings that come through Ahura Mazda's rule.

Salvation is taught through the wisdom Ahura Mazda conceived in accordance with Asha and through the inspired words of Good Mind. It is contrasted with the fate of those who follow the Lie and the wicked.

Yasna LII (Sp. LI) presents A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits. The speaker prays for benefits, goodness, and sanctity for the entire creation of the holy and the clean, including present, emerging, and future generations. Sanctity is described as bringing prosperity, shelter, healing virtue, good gifts, and success while overcoming the harmful malice of the Daêvas. The prayer also concerns the sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise of the Bountiful Immortals, the prosperity of the holy creation, and opposition to the entire evil creation through Righteousness.

l: Yasna LII (Sp. LI), Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: Yasna LII (Sp. LI) contains A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits. It describes prayers for sanctity, prosperity, healing virtue, and protection from the Daêvas.

l: A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits, Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits asks for goodness, benefits, and sanctity for present, emerging, and future generations. It also seeks prosperity for the holy creation and opposition to the entire evil creation.
Sanctity is prayed for as a source of prosperity and long-lasting shelter. It brings healing virtue, good gifts, blessings, and success, and it overwhelms the harmful malice of the Daêvas.

Benefits are requested for the entire creation of the holy and the clean, including present, emerging, and future generations. The greatest, best, and most beautiful benefits are associated with sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and prosperity.

l: entire creation, Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: The entire creation of the holy is prayed for benefits, goodness, prosperity, and sanctity. Its prosperity is set in opposition to the entire evil creation.
Prosperity is presented as accompanying sanctity and receiving shelter from it. The prayer seeks prosperity for the abode, the entire creation of the holy, and the clean.

l: healing virtue, Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: Healing virtue is described as coming in waters, belonging to cattle, or being found in plants. It is borne by sanctity as a benefit.
The Daêvas and their servants are described as possessing harmful malice that might harm the dwelling and its lord. Sanctity overwhelms that harmful malice.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are the subjects of sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise in the prayer.

l: the entire evil creation, Yasna, Yasna LII (Sp. LI).
s: The entire evil creation is opposed as the counterpart of the prosperity sought for the entire creation of the holy and the clean.
Righteousness is the means through which the speaker praises. The speaker identifies as beneficent and chooses those who are likewise of a better mind.

Yasna LIII. concerns the answered prayer of Zarathustra Spitâma, the devotion of Kavi Vîstâspa, Zarathustra Spitâma, and Frashaostra, and the founding of the Faith of the Saoshyant by Ahura Mazda. It presents marriage counsel for Pourukista and for maidens, bride and bridegroom, emphasizing mutual care in Righteousness and service to the Good Mind, Asha, and Mazda. It describes the protection of the faithful from the Lie-demon, the role of righteous women in overcoming temptation, and the defeat of sinners and deceivers. It concludes by affirming Ahura Mazda’s power, Kingdom, and highest blessings for the right-living poor.
Yasna LIII. presents prayers, religious devotion, marriage counsel, protection from the Lie-demon, and the defeat of sinners and deceivers.
Zarathustra Spitâma offers prayer and propitiation to Ahura Mazda and is associated with the good Faith’s disciples in word and deed. Zarathustra Spitâma is also identified as Pourukista’s father.

Ahura Mazda grants the boons sought in Zarathustra Spitâma’s prayer, including prospered eternal life and faithful disciples. Ahura Mazda will found the Faith of the Saoshyant and possesses the power and Kingdom that bestow the highest blessings on the right-living poor.

l: Faith of the Saoshyant, Yasna, Yasna LIII.
s: The Faith of the Saoshyant is a faith that Ahura Mazda will found. Kavi Vîstâspa, Zarathustra Spitâma, and Frashaostra offer praise and Yasna confessions while making straight paths for it.

Pourukista, a young daughter of Zarathustra, is given a husband as a help in the true service of the Good Mind, Asha, and Mazda. Pourukista is instructed to counsel well with her husband and act with just action.
The Good Mind is served truly by Pourukista and her husband. Its bright blessing is sought for the master and toilers, and its life is presented as a goal obtained through the laws of the Faith.
Asha is served by Pourukista and the husband given to her. Asha is also invoked with the Good Mind and Mazda in the context of marriage and righteous action.
The Lie-demon is opposed and guarded against. Its hate and the hate of its bondsmen are prayed away from the body, and its courses are said to destroy mental life.

Righteous women receive recompense for their great cause. Although lustful desire descends toward the spirit of evil, righteous women bring forth the champion who helps the cause and conquers temptation.
Maidens are given monitions for marrying and urged to heed the laws of the Faith so that they may obtain the life of the Good Mind on earth and in heaven.

l: bride and bridegroom, Yasna, Yasna LIII.
s: Bride and bridegroom are instructed to cherish each other in Righteousness. Their mutual care is presented as the condition for a happy home-life.
The Kingdom belongs to Ahura Mazda. Through the Kingdom, Ahura Mazda bestows the highest blessings on the right-living poor.

Marriage counsel teaches maidens, bride, and bridegroom to follow the laws of the Faith and to cherish one another in Righteousness. It also directs couples to counsel together with the mind of Ârmaiti and to act justly.
Home-life is said to be happy when bride and bridegroom cherish each other in Righteousness. Peace is also sought for dwellings and hamlets.

l: prayer of Zarathustra, Yasna, Yasna LIII.
s: The prayer of Zarathustra Spitâma is answered by Ahura Mazda. It asks for boons flowing from the good Order, including a prospered life of eternal duration and the conversion of deceivers into disciples of the good Faith.

Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII), titled The Airyemâ-Ishyô, concerns prayers and sacrifices connected with the Airyaman and the Airyemâ-ishyô. It asks that the Airyaman draw near to the men and women taught of Zarathustra for the joyful grace of the Good Mind. It seeks the sacred reward of the ritual order and asks that Ahura Mazda grant or increase it. It also sacrifices to the powerful Airyemâ-ishyô, the bounteous Gâthas, and the Praises of the Yasna.

l: Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII), Yasna, Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII).
s: Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII) is titled The Airyemâ-Ishyô. It contains prayers for grace and sacred reward, and sacrifices to the Airyemâ-ishyô, the Gâthas, and the Praises of the Yasna.
The Airyemâ-ishyô is described as powerful, victoriously smiting, opposed to assaulting malice, and the greatest of the sentences of the holy ritual order. It receives sacrifice.
The Airyaman is described as the desired friend and peers-man. It is asked to draw near for grace to the men and women who are taught of Zarathustra.

l: Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII).
s: The Good Mind is associated with joyful grace. Its grace enables the conscience to attain its wished-for recompense.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII).
s: The ritual order is connected with a sacred reward that is desired. Its greatest sentence is identified with the Airyemâ-ishyô, and Ahura Mazda is asked to grant or increase its reward.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII).
s: Ahura Mazda is asked to grant or cause to increase the sacred reward of the ritual order.
The Gâthas are described as bounteous and as ruling supreme in the holy and august ritual. They receive sacrifice.

Yasna LV (Sp. LIV) concerns the conclusion of the worship of the Gâthas and the beginning of that of the Staota Yêsnya. We offer our riches, persons, bodies, consciousness, souls, and Fravashi to the bountiful Gâthas and worship them with the divine Righteousness and the Good Mind. The Gâthas are described as guardians, defenders, and spiritual food and clothing for souls, bringing rewards, health, protection, progress, sanctity, and gifts. The unit also worships the Praises of the Yasna in their remembered, recited, learned, taught, repeated, chanted, and offered forms, which further the world through grace.

l: Yasna LV (Sp. LIV), Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: Yasna LV (Sp. LIV) concerns the worship of the Gâthas as concluded and that of the Staota Yêsnya as beginning.

The Gâthas receive as an offering all landed riches, persons, bones and tissues, forms and forces, consciousness, soul, and Fravashi. They are worshipped as bountiful, ruling as the leading chants within the holy ritual, and as sources of protection, nourishment, rewards, health, progress, growth, sanctity, and gifts.

l: Staota Yêsnya, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The Staota Yêsnya is identified as beginning in this unit.
We present our riches and ourselves as an offering to the Gâthas, worship the divine Righteousness, the Good Mind, and the Gâthas, and worship the Praises of the Yasna in their various forms.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: Mazda is described as the most beneficent, producing the Praises of the Offering, victorious when He smites, and helping the settlements advance.
Asha is addressed as abiding within the Gâthas and is asked to give blessings to every holy man who comes with the prayer and endeavors to help himself according to good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The Good Mind is worshipped together with the divine Righteousness and the bountiful Gâthas.

l: Gâthas as guardians and spiritual food, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The Gâthas are described as guardians and defenders and as spiritual food and clothing for souls. They are asked to be abundant givers of rewards for the world beyond the present.

l: religious order of the settlements, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The religious order of the settlements is to be protected and guarded by the victorious and beneficent effects associated with the Gâthas and the Praises of the Offering.
Mazda helps the settlements advance, and the Praises of the Offering are associated with protecting present settlements and those that shall bring salvation.

l: entire creation, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The entire creation of the holy and the clean is to receive protection through the Praises of the Offering.

l: Praises of the Offering, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The Praises of the Offering are asked to appear with power, victory, health, healing, progress, growth, preparation, protection, beneficence, sanctity, and abundant gifts toward those who can understand.

l: Praises of the Yasna, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The Praises of the Yasna are worshipped as productions of the ancient world that are recollected, learned, taught, held in mind, repeated, remembered, recited, and worshipped. Their recitation, memorised recital, chanting, and complete offering are also worshipped because they further the world through grace.
The Yasna is associated with praises that are remembered, recited, learned, taught, repeated, chanted, and offered, and whose grace furthers the world.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The holy ritual contains appointed times and seasons within which the Gâthas rule as the leading chants.
Worship is directed toward the divine Righteousness, the Good Mind, the Gâthas, and the Praises of the Yasna, including their recitation, chanting, and complete offering.

l: act of homage, Yasna, Yasna LV (Sp. LIV).
s: The offering consists of all landed riches and the persons, bodies, consciousness, souls, and Fravashi of those presenting it. The Praises of the Yasna are also worshipped in their complete offering.

Yasna LVI (Sp. LV) introduces the Srôsh Yast. It repeatedly calls for Sraosha, identified with attentive or listening Obedience, to be present for the worship of Ahura Mazda, the good waters, the Fravashis of the saints and their souls, the good and bountiful Immortals, and Blessedness. Sraosha is described as good, holy, blessed, and stately, and as one who smites with victory and furthers settlements in their advance.

l: Yasna LVI (Sp. LV), Yasna, Yasna LVI (Sp. LV).
s: Yasna LVI (Sp. LV) introduces the Srôsh Yast and contains invocations of Sraosha for worship.

l: The Srôsh Yast, Yasna, Yasna LVI (Sp. LV).
s: The Srôsh Yast is introduced in this unit as the subject of the text.

Sraosha is identified with listening or attentive Obedience and is repeatedly invoked to be present for worship. Sraosha is associated with Ahura Mazda, the good waters, the Fravashis of the saints and their souls, the good and bountiful Immortals, and Blessedness. Sraosha is described as good, holy, blessed, and stately, as one who smites with victory and furthers settlements in their advance.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LVI (Sp. LV).
s: Ahura Mazda is described as the most beneficent and holy, and as desired by worshippers at the first and at the last. Sraosha is invoked to be present for the worship of Ahura Mazda.
Worship in this unit is directed toward Ahura Mazda, the good waters, the Fravashis of the saints and their souls, the good and bountiful Immortals, Blessedness, and Sraosha.

Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI), called The Srôsh Yast, concerns worship and praise of Sraosha, or Obedience the blessed. Sraosha is described as a victorious ritual lord who protects settlements, guards Ahura Mazda’s creatures, battles the Daêvas, and aids the righteous. The text recounts Sraosha’s association with Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the Bountiful Immortals, Haoma, the Gâthas, and the Mãthra. It asks Sraosha to protect people in both the corporeal and mental worlds and to grant strength, soundness, speed, and victory.

l: Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI)., Yasna, Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI).
s: Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI) is presented as a unit of worship and praise for Sraosha, or Obedience the blessed. It describes his victories, guardianship, ritual authority, and protection of people and settlements.

l: The Srôsh Yast, Yasna, Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI).
s: The Srôsh Yast is the title given to Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI). It consists of praises, acts of worship, and petitions directed to Sraosha.

Sraosha is worshipped as Obedience the blessed, the stately and victorious ritual lord who furthers settlements. He guards Ahura Mazda’s creatures, battles the Daêvas, protects houses and people, and is asked to grant speed, soundness, vigilance, and victory.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped together with Sraosha and is described as the lofty Lord who has approached nearest to the ritual celebrations. His creation is associated with the first worship performed by Sraosha, and his creatures are guarded by Sraosha.
Zarathustra is associated with the five Gâthas, which Sraosha is said to have first chanted. His words and deeds are worshipped as part of the ritual.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped and praised in connection with Sraosha’s first ritual acts, the Baresman, and the Gâthas. Sraosha sits among them as a companion at their meeting.
The Daêvas are opposed by Sraosha, who battles them, guards against them, and causes them to turn in fear. He is also said to cleave their skulls and hew down the Daêvas of Mazendran.

Haraiti is described as high and lofty, with Sraosha’s house standing on its highest height. Haoma worshipped Sraosha there, and the house is described as self-lighted within and star-studded without.
The Mãthra is identified as Sraosha’s body. Sraosha is also described as possessing the first place in the Mãthra.
The Gâthas are the five Gâthas of Zarathustra, whose metres, words, Zand, questions, and answers Sraosha is said to have first chanted.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI).
s: Righteousness is called the Best in the opening blessing. It is also named among the religious principles confessed with Ahura Mazda and the Good Mind.

Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII), called The Fshûshô-Mãthra, presents worship as protection from the Daêva and the evil-minded man. It entrusts settlements and persons to worship for protection, care, guarding, and oversight, and connects worship with Blessedness, Piety, and good thoughts, words, and deeds. The unit praises the owner of herds, asks the Bountiful Immortals to save holy men and saintly women, and offers thoughts, words, actions, herds, and men to the Bountiful Spirit. It also praises Ahura Mazda, the Righteous Order, the Fire of Ahura Mazda, and the Praises of the Yasna.

l: Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII), Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII) is identified as The Fshûshô-Mãthra. It presents worship as protection, entrusts settlements and persons to its care, and offers praise to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the Fire of Ahura Mazda, and the Praises of the Yasna.

l: The Fshûshô-Mãthra, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: The Fshûshô-Mãthra describes worship as a shelter from the Daêva and the evil-minded man. It praises the owner of herds, asks for salvation and protection, and offers thoughts, words, actions, herds, and men to the Bountiful Spirit.

Worship is offered as a service whose results include Blessedness, Piety, well-thought thought, the word well spoken, and the deed well done. Settlements and persons are entrusted to it for protection, care, guarding, and oversight, and choices are exercised in it.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: Ahura Mazda is addressed as the one with whom the worshippers abide and to whom they belong. He is called the Creator, and His creative stars are asked to shine upon and around the worshippers with healthy herds, healthy settlements, healthy men, vigour, and blessing.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are asked to save holy men and saintly women and to rule and dispose aright. Their Righteousness is invoked as the means of salvation, and their greatness, goodness, and spiritual beauty are rendered through the owner of herds.

l: owner of herds, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: The owner of herds is called righteous, victorious when he strikes, and the best. He is described as the father of the Kine, the holy man, and the sanctified creation, and as a bestower of blessings and a guardian together with the Righteous Order.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: The Righteous Order is associated with the protection and guarding provided by the owner of herds. It is also invoked with the Bountiful Immortals as part of the means by which the worshippers are saved.
The Fire of Ahura Mazda is praised and asked to come for help in the great effort and for the joy-producing grace of the great interest of the cause. It is asked to grant both Weal and Deathlessness.

l: Praises of the Yasna, Yasna, Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII).
s: The Praises of the Yasna are described as having a careful structure of language that has reached its object. The worshippers sacrifice to their entire collection and offer homage to the most beautiful forms of Ahura Mazda, including the stars and the highest of the high.

Yasna LIX, also called Sp. LVIII, is titled “Mutual Blessings.” It concerns worship of Verethraghna, Saoshyant, the Baresman, souls, and Fravashis, followed by blessings spoken by the Ratu and Zaotar. It also praises Ahû, Ratu, Mazda, Asha, Asha Vahista, the Fshûshô-mãthra, and the Yasna Praises.

l: Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII), Yasna, Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII).
s: Yasna LIX, also called Sp. LVIII, contains the section titled “Mutual Blessings.” It includes worship, spoken blessings, and concluding praises.

l: Mutual Blessings, Yasna, Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII).
s: “Mutual Blessings” is the title of this unit. The Ratu gives a blessing to the Zaotar, and the Zaotar returns a blessing.
Verethraghna is worshiped as the Ahura-made, victorious blow.
Saoshyant is worshiped as the one who smites with victory.
The Baresman is sacrificed to with its Zaothra and its girdle, which is its band, and it is spread with sanctity.

The Ratu speaks a blessing wishing the good servant of the Lord what is better than the good, acquisition of what is their own in the Zaothra, and the reward obtained by the Zaotar. The Ratu is also described as one who rules from Righteousness.

The Zaotar is described as far advanced in good thoughts, words, and deeds. The Zaotar receives the Ratu’s blessing and responds by wishing what is better than the good and rejecting what is worse than the evil.
Ahû is described as excellent in the formula beginning, “As our Ahû is excellent.”

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII).
s: Asha is called the Best and is presented as a blessing.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII).
s: Mazda is associated with actions done for Mazda and with the Kingdom belonging to Ahura, which offers a nurturer to the poor.

l: Asha Vahista, Yasna, Yasna LIX (Sp. LVIII).
s: Asha Vahista is worshiped as the most beautiful, Bountiful Immortal.
The Yasna is praised through worship of the entire collection of its Praises and the Yasna Praises instituted in the world of yore.
Righteousness is identified with the rule of the Ratu in the statement that the Ratu rules from his Righteousness.

Yasna LX (Sp. LIX) concerns prayers for the dwelling of the sacrificer. It asks for blessings, prosperity, righteous order, divine sovereignty, the Zarathustrian Faith, and the presence of holy beings within the house. It calls for obedience, peace, generosity, reverence, and truthful speech to overcome their opposites. It concludes by asking that the sacrificers attain Heaven, the best world of the saints, and companionship with Ahura Mazda.

l: Yasna LX (Sp. LIX), Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: Yasna LX (Sp. LIX) is a prayer for the dwelling of the sacrificer. It invokes blessings, protection, prosperity, righteous order, and eventual attainment of Heaven.

l: house of the sacrificer, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The house is asked to receive blessings, wise perceptions, righteous order, divine sovereignty, prosperity, holy strength, and the Fravashis of the saints. Obedience, peace, generosity, reverence, and truthful speech are to prevail within it.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: Ahura Mazda is addressed as the Great giver Lord and is asked to grant approach to the good, divine blessings, and eventual companionship with Him.
The saints are associated with wise perceptions, sacred blessings, guileless characteristics, and recognition of what is due. Their Fravashis are asked to come to the house and aid the better men.
The Righteous Order is asked to appear for the village and to gain victory over the Demon of the Lie. It is also praised as the best, most beautiful, and bounteous Immortal.

l: Zarathustrian Faith, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The Zarathustrian Faith is described as Ahura's Religion, whose long enduring prominence is desired within the house.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The good, heroic, and bountiful Fravashis of the saints are asked to come to the house and go hand in hand with the worshippers. Their healing gifts are associated with the furtherance of better men, hindrance of the hostile, and growth of riches and glory.
Sraosha, identified as Obedience, is asked to conquer disobedience within the house. He is also described as governing there and as receiving good Yasnas and praises.

l: Demon of the Lie, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The Demon of the Lie is to be defeated by the Righteous Order.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The Bountiful Immortals seek good Yasnas, good praises, and good sacrifices and acts of homage for salvation. Their desired offerings include a long continued offering of the entire self.
Heaven is the destination to which the glorified bodies are asked to go openly as the best world of the saints devoted to Ahura.

l: best world of the saints, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: The best world of the saints is identified with the destination of glorified bodies and is described as devoted to Ahura.

l: Asha Vahista, Yasna, Yasna LX (Sp. LIX).
s: Asha Vahista, identified as Righteousness the Best, is asked to accompany the worshippers as they approach and come around Ahura Mazda.

The unit concerns sending forth the Ahuna-vairya, Asha Vahista, YêNhê hâtãm, and the prayer of the pious man between heaven and earth. It calls for encounter with and displacement of Angra Mainyu, Kahvaredha, Kayadhas, thieves, robbers, Zandas, sorcerers, covenant breakers, and others opposed to the holy ritual laws. It also calls for the overthrow of murderers of the saints, persecutors, ritual opponents, the tyrant full of death, and the wicked. Zarathustra Spitama and the prophets who are yet to serve and save thy people are concerned with driving the Demon of the Lie from the seven Karshvars and dislodging the entire evil world.
The Ahuna-vairya is to be pealed forth in the liturgy between heaven and earth.

l: Asha Vahista, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: Asha Vahista is to be sent forth in prayer between heaven and earth.

l: YêNhê hâtãm, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: YêNhê hâtãm is to be sent forth in the liturgy between heaven and earth.

l: good and pious Prayer for blessings, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The prayer of the pious man is sent forth for blessings and for encounter with and displacement of evil powers and beings.
Encounter is sought with Angra Mainyu, Kahvaredha, Kayadhas, and other evil or hostile beings.
Displacement is sought against Angra Mainyu and his creatures, including Kahvaredha and Kayadhas.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: Angra Mainyu is described as filled with death for those whom he has made, and his encounter and displacement are sought.
Kahvaredha and the individual Kahvaredhas, male and female, are named as targets for encounter and dislodgment.
The Kayadhas and the individual Kayadhians, male and female, are named as targets for encounter and dislodgment.

l: murderers of the saints, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The murderers of the saints are named as targets for encounter and overthrow.

l: the wicked, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The wicked are to be pealed forth for encounter and overthrow if their thoughts, words, and works are not congenial to the holy ritual laws.
Zarathustra Spitama is addressed in connection with the overthrow of the wicked.

l: holy ritual laws, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The holy ritual laws are the standard against which the thoughts, words, and works of the wicked are judged.

l: Demon of the Lie, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The Demon of the Lie is to be driven from hence from the prophets and from the seven Karshvars.

l: prophets who are yet to serve and save thy people, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The prophets who are yet to serve and save thy people are to drive the Demon of the Lie away, gaining power over her as being utterly without power.

l: evil world, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The entire evil world is to be dislodged.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LXI (Sp. LX).
s: The ritual is persecuted by some, and those who persecute it are named as targets for encounter and overthrow.
Overthrow is sought against murderers of the saints, persecutors, the tyrant full of death, and the wicked.
Dislodgment is sought against Kahvaredha, Kayadhas, the Demon of the Lie, and the entire evil world.

This unit concerns the Fire, addressed as Ahura Mazda's son, and the offerings, care, blessings, and admonitions associated with it. The man who worships the Fire is promised salvation when he approaches it truthfully with wood, Baresman, flesh, and a mortar. The Fire is asked to remain aflame and growing in the house until the heroic renovation is complete, and to grant glory, nourishment, booty, understanding, power, and a capable offspring. The Fire blesses those who bring properly prepared wood and other sacred materials, while Ahura Mazda's Fire addresses an admonition to those for whom it cooks meals.

The Fire is offered sacrifice, homage, praise, benedictions, wood, perfume, sacred butter, and properly placed andirons. It is asked to remain aflame, shining, and growing in the house, and to grant glory, nourishment, booty, understanding, power, instructors, good reward, good renown, and preparation of the soul. The Fire examines those who approach it, blesses the person who brings properly prepared wood or sacred plants, and gives blessings concerning cattle, people, an active mind and soul, and a blest life.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXII (Sp. LXI).
s: Ahura Mazda's son is another designation for the Fire. Ahura Mazda's Fire gives blessings to the person who brings it properly prepared wood and addresses an admonition to those for whom it cooks the night and morning meal.

l: man who worships the Fire, Yasna, Yasna LXII (Sp. LXI).
s: The man who worships the Fire in verity and truth approaches it with wood in hand, Baresman ready, flesh in hand, and a mortar. Salvation is promised to him, and the Fire blesses him if he brings properly prepared wood or other sacred materials.
Salvation is promised to the man who worships the Fire in verity and truth while bringing the prescribed ritual materials.

Wood is to feed the Fire according to prescription. The Fire blesses the person who brings wood that is well dried, sought out for flaming, and purified with the earnest blessing of the sacred ritual truth.

l: heroic renovation, Yasna, Yasna LXII (Sp. LXI).
s: The Fire is asked to remain aflame, shining, and growing in the house for the furtherance of the heroic renovation and until the good heroic time when the renovation has become complete.

The requested offspring is to be sure of foot, wakeful, quick to rise, helpful to nurture or reclaim, legitimate, orderly in men's meetings, influential in assemblies, powerful, skilled, and able to redeem others from oppression. Such offspring is also asked to advance the speaker's line, Vîs, Zantu, and province, and to deliver orders to the Province as firm and righteous rulers.

l: Yasna, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV) praises Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and the waters for their healing, purifying, life-sustaining, and prosperity-bringing powers. It describes the waters flowing from Hukairya to the sea Vouru-kasha, dividing toward the seven Karshvars, and purifying the seed, wombs, and milk of women. The text excludes evil people from the waters’ benefits and prescribes the proper invocations and offerings taught by Ahura Mazda through Zarathustra. It asks the waters and many holy beings to grant wealth, worthy offspring, Immortality, and Welfare.

l: Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV), Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV) praises Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and the waters, describes their powers and courses, and sets out prayers and offerings to them. It asks for wealth, worthy offspring, Immortality, and Welfare.

l: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is praised as wide-flowing, healing, efficacious against the Daêvas, devoted to Ahura's lore, and beneficial to living things, herds, settlements, wealth, and the Province. She purifies the seed of male beings, sanctifies women's wombs, makes women fortunate in labour, and provides a regular and timely flow of milk. Her waters flow from high Hukairya to the sea Vouru-kasha, with a thousand tributaries and a thousand outlets, and one chief outlet divides toward the seven Karshvars.

l: waters, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: The waters are praised as good, Mazda-made, holy, and purifying. They are called upon to withhold their benefits from evildoers and to come as torments against those who harm settlements, bodies, disciples, or kindred. They are to receive a first petition and sanctified Zaothras delivered according to the ritual taught by the Aêthrapaiti.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Ahura Mazda showed Zarathustra how to pray and offer to the waters, and Zarathustra taught this to the corporeal worlds. Ahura Mazda is asked to grant Immortality and Welfare through the Good Mind in the doctrine.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: The saints’ Fravashis, including those of the living, the dead, the born, and the yet unborn, are invited to draw near. They are described as having borne the waters upstream from the nearest waters below.

l: Zarathustra, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Zarathustra is instructed to pray the first petition to the waters, offer sanctified Zaothras, and pronounce the prescribed words. He taught the corporeal worlds what Ahura Mazda had shown him.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are addressed as ruling and disposing aright. They are asked to grant wealth and offspring.

l: the Yazads, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: The Yazads are addressed as holy beings who rule mightily and possess power. They are asked to grant what is greater, better, more beautiful, and more precious, including Immortality and Welfare.

l: eternal Immortality, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Immortality is identified with Welfare as a gift greater, better, more beautiful, and more precious than the requested wealth and offspring. It is requested from the Yazads and from Ahura Mazda.

l: Weal, Yasna, Yasna LXIII (Sp. LXII). / Yasna LXIV (Sp. LXIII). / Yasna LXV (Sp. LXIV).
s: Welfare is identified with Immortality as an eternal gift. It is requested from the Yazads and from Ahura Mazda as that which most promotes the petitioners' well-being.

Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV) concerns an offering addressed to the Ahurian One. The speaker offers the Zaothra with sanctity, together with the Haoma and the flesh, and the Hadhânaêpata lifted up with sacred regularity. The offering is made for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha (Obedience) the blessed, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.

l: Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV), Yasna, Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV).
s: Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV) presents an offering addressed to the Ahurian One and made for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha (Obedience) the blessed, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.

l: Ahurian One, Yasna, Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV).
s: The Ahurian One is addressed as the recipient of the Zaothra, which is offered with sanctity together with the Haoma and the flesh.
The Zaothra is offered with sanctity. It is offered together with the Haoma and the flesh, and with the Hadhânaêpata lifted up with sacred regularity.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV).
s: Ahura Mazda is named as one for whose propitiation the offering is made. The Fire of Ahura Mazda is also named among those connected with the offering.
Propitiation is the purpose of the offering. The offering seeks the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha (Obedience) the blessed, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.

Yasna LXVII (Sp. LXVI) is identified as a unit of text. Sections 1-4 refer to Y. XXIII, 1-4, with “I desire to approach with sanctity” replaced by “I offer with sanctity,” and also refer to Y. VII, 24. Sections 5-7 refer to Y. XXXVIII, 3-5.

l: Yasna LXVII (Sp. LXVI), Yasna, Yasna LXVII (Sp. LXVI).
s: Yasna LXVII (Sp. LXVI) contains sections 1-4 that refer to Y. XXIII, 1-4, with “I desire to approach with sanctity” replaced by “I offer with sanctity,” and also refer to Y. VII, 24. Its sections 5-7 refer to Y. XXXVIII, 3-5.

The unit concerns offerings and prayers to the Ahurian One, Ahura Mazda, the Zaothra, and the good waters. The worshippers ask for health, healing, growth, prosperity, offspring, protection, glory, and the best life of the saints. The waters are praised as those created by Mazda and are invoked to support fertility, plants, settlements, and worshippers. The unit also concerns the Yasna, the Mazdayasnians who perform it, and blessings for villages through the Good Mind and Righteous Order.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXVIII (Sp. LXVII).
s: Ahura Mazda is praised together with the Bountiful Immortals and is identified as the creator of the good waters. The worshippers ask Ahura Mazda to cause them to prosper to salvation through the Good Mind, the Sovereign Power, and the Righteous Order.

l: Ahurian One (Ahura Mazda), Yasna, Yasna LXVIII (Sp. LXVII).
s: The Ahurian One is addressed as the recipient of offerings and Yasna. The worshippers ask the Ahurian One for heaven, legitimate offspring, prosperity, protection, healing, and assistance, and seek its presence at their Yasna.

The waters are worshipped as the sea Vouru-kasha and all waters upon earth, including standing, running, well, spring, rain, and canal waters. They are asked to grant splendour, glory, health, vigour, possessions, offspring, long life, and the best life of the saints.
The Zaothra is offered to the Ahurian One with Haoma, milk, and Hadhânaêpata. It is invoked for health, healing, progress, growth, ceremonial merit, good renown, equanimity, and victory.

The Yasna is offered as a legitimate act of worship and homage because of Righteousness the Best. It is used to invoke the waters, seek blessings, support settlements, and request prosperity to salvation.

The Mazdayasnians are described as offering sacrifice together with colleagues, disciples, men, women, children, and maidens. They ask for the desire and knowledge of the straightest path, the overwhelming of oppression and malice, and the best life of the saints.

The village from which the Zaothras come is the subject of a benediction for a safe, quiet, joyful, and long abode. Every Mazdayasnian village is likewise given a prayer for safety, joy, longevity, succour, salutations of salvation, and praises.

l: Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna LXVIII (Sp. LXVII).
s: The Good Mind is named as a means through which the worshippers may prosper to salvation. It is invoked together with the Sovereign Power and the Righteous Order.

l: Righteous Order, Yasna, Yasna LXVIII (Sp. LXVII).
s: The Righteous Order is associated with the straightest path and the best life of the saints. It is named with the Good Mind and Sovereign Power as a means of prosperity to salvation and is praised as the basis of the excellent Ratu's rule.
Yasna LXIX (Sp. LXVIII) is identified as a chapter. The chapter is composed of fragments. It refers to Y. XV, 2, and Y. LI, 1 and 22.

l: Yasna LXIX (Sp. LXVIII), Yasna, Yasna LXIX (Sp. LXVIII).
s: Yasna LXIX (Sp. LXVIII) is a chapter composed of fragments. It refers to Y. XV, 2, and Y. LI, 1 and 22.

The unit concerns worship of the Bountiful Immortals, especially Ahura Mazda, and Zarathustra Spitâma. It declares the institutions associated with Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Asha Vahista, Khshatra-vairya, Bountiful Âramaiti, Weal and Immortality, the Kine, Fire, and other sacred beings and prayers. It seeks good religious speech, prophetic service, good thoughts, words, and deeds, and praises the good waters, Apãm-napât, and Sraosha.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LXX (Sp. LXIX).
s: They are worshipped with sacrifice as those who rule aright and dispose of all aright.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXX (Sp. LXIX).
s: He is especially approached with praise and worshipped as the deity and lord who is the Creator, gracious helper, and maker of all good things. Institutions associated with him are declared.
He is worshipped with sacrifice as the chieftain of the rite.

l: institutions of religion, Yasna, Yasna LXX (Sp. LXIX).
s: They are declared as established, exact, and undeviating. The unit includes institutions associated with Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Asha Vahista, Khshatra-vairya, Bountiful Âramaiti, Weal and Immortality, the Kine, Fire, Sraosha, Rashnu, Mithra, Wind, the good Mazdayasnian Religion, and various prayers.

l: Good Mind, Yasna, Yasna LXX (Sp. LXIX).
s: Its institutions are declared, and the speakers ask that it approach them so that their souls may advance in good.
He is described as blessed Obedience and is invoked to aid the worship. He is also worshipped with sacrifice.

Yasna LXXI concerns Frashaostra’s question to Zarathustra about the memorised recital of the rites and the completed delivery of the Gâthas. Zarathustra answers by describing sacrifices and worship directed to Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the Fravashis, the Bountiful Immortals, the Yazads, the Mazdayasnian Faith, the Gâthas, and the holy creation. Ahura Mazda promises that whoever pronounces the prescribed words at the last ending of life will have the soul kept away from Hell, cross the Kinvat Bridge in holiness, and enter Heaven. The unit also praises the Yasna, its ending words, its Gâthas, and the Staota-Yêsnya hymns.
Frashaostra, the holy, asks Zarathustra what the memorised recital of the rites and the completed delivery of the Gâthas are.
Zarathustra answers Frashaostra by reciting the rites and sacrifices. He is worshipped as a holy lord of the ritual order, and he is told to pronounce certain words at the last ending of life.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the holy lord of the ritual order and as the skilful maker of creation. He promises to keep the soul away from Hell if the prescribed words are pronounced at the last ending of life.
The Yasna is worshipped in its entirety, including its sacred metres, praises, words, ending words, and Praise-songs.

l: Yasna LXXI, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: Yasna LXXI is the Yasna Concluding and presents the completed recital of the rites and the delivery of the Gâthas.
The five Gâthas are worshipped as holy and bountiful. Their ending words and hymns are sacrificed to, and the Gâtha Ustavaiti is to be intoned as a salvation hail.

l: Fravashi of Zarathustra, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The Fravashi of Zarathustra, the saint, is included among those to whom sacrifice is offered.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The good, heroic, and bounteous Fravashis of the saints are worshipped and sacrificed to, including those of the bodily and mental worlds, houses, villages, districts, provinces, and the Zarathustrôtemas.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped as guardians of the saints and as the entire body of Ahura Mazda’s holy order.

l: the Yazads, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The Yazads, lords of the ritual order, are worshipped and sacrificed to. The unit especially mentions the most strenuous Yazad and several named Yazads, including Apãm-napât and Nairya-sangha.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The entire Mazdayasnian Faith is sacrificed to and worshipped, including its system set up against the Daêvas.
The entire bounteous Mãthra is worshipped together with its complete and long descent.

l: words which Mazda spake, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The words which Mazda spake are sacrificed to because they are most fatal to evil thoughts, words, and deeds. Their strength, victory, glory, and speed are also invoked.

l: evil thought, word, and deed, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The evil thought, word, and deed are designated and then cut down and felled by the words which Mazda spake.
Heaven is the place into which the holy person comes after crossing the Kinvat Bridge, and the soul is promised entry there.

l: Kinvat Bridge, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The Kinvat Bridge is crossed by the soul in holiness when the person has acted and spoken as prescribed.
